judge_assessment.explanation: ACCEPT is right and every solution the judge lists is confirmed: x<5, n>=8, x<=-5, x>5, m<=6, x<-4, y>-5, w<=-3, x>-6, m>=7, t<=9, x<=-4, each matching its verify.json triple including the open/closed endpoint token and the shading direction. Problem 12's written explanation IS honestly declared -- verify.json id 12 carries a second entry {"type": "manual", "desc": "Explain in a sentence why dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality sign"}, the build exits 2, and the key states the full-credit criterion and rejects the shallow version ('"You forgot to flip" names the rule but not the reason --- push for the second half'). Where I part company is the severity of the Quick Answers finding. The judge calls it 'several open-endpoint tokens rendered awkwardly as literal implementation text', which reads like a typography nit. What actually prints on entries 1, 4, 6, 7 and 9 is '<built-in function open>'. I traced it: render_quick_answers._fmt() renders string expecteds as sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)), and sympy.sympify('open') resolves to PYTHON'S BUILT-IN open FUNCTION, whose latex is '\mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}' -- I confirmed both at the interpreter. So the bank is not awkward, it is printing a Python repr, and it does so because a data token is being evaluated against builtins. The remaining seven entries are no better for a grader: they read '-inf, -3, closed' and '8, inf, closed' -- raw interval triples -- where the key's own boxed answers read w <= -3 and n >= 8. The bank is unusable across all twelve entries, not five. Second omission: answer_key.tex contains ZERO tikzpicture environments while worksheet.tex contains 24, so a sheet whose every problem says 'Solve and graph' ships a key that draws no graph at all and describes each one in prose instead. Neither defect overturns ACCEPT, but neither is cosmetic.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 10 and 11 are the pattern the rest of this shard should copy. Both say 'Write a one-step inequality ... solve it, and graph', and the verify entry is type `inequality` with expr '8*t - 72' and relation '<=' -- so the RELATION the student was asked to write is part of the check, not just the solution value. Where sister cases got rejected for verifying only the solution of a 'write and solve' item, this encoding actually covers the written form.

The endpoint semantics are encoded, not implied: every expected is a [lower, upper, open|closed] triple, so the open circle versus solid dot and the shading direction are machine-recorded per problem rather than left to the key's prose. That is why the judge could confirm all twelve graphs against the data.

Problem 8 (6w <= -18) exists purely to separate 'the answer is negative' from 'you divided by a negative', and the stem says so ('The answer here is negative, but nothing in the solving step is'). The key closes the loop: 'Common wrong answer: w >= -3 --- flipped because a negative number appeared somewhere. The rule keys on what you divide by, not on the sign of the answer.'

Problem 12's manual item is handled the way every open response in this shard should be: declared {"type": "manual"} with a desc, the build exiting 2, the key labelling it 'Part of this problem is an open explanation, flagged for manual review', supplying model wording, AND stating what falls short of full credit. It also gives the reason behind the rule ('3 > 1, but -3 < -1'), not just the rule.

Problems 6 and 9 both close with a substitution audit the student can run alone -- problem 6's 'Test x = 0: -2(0) = 0, and 0 > 8 is false, so 0 must not be in the solution --- which rules the un-flipped answer out immediately'. That converts the flip rule from something remembered into something checkable.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt() evaluates every string expected with sympy.sympify(), which falls through to Python's builtins when the token is not a symbol it recognises. The endpoint token 'open' therefore resolves to the built-in open() function and typesets as '<built-in function open>' in the printed answer key. The sibling token 'closed' escapes only by accident -- there is no builtin of that name, so it becomes a plain Symbol.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers entries 1, 4, 6, 7, 9 print '<built-in function open>' (extracted as '¡built-in function open¿' because \text-mode < and > mangle in OT1)
verify.json ids 1, 4, 6, 7, 9 all carry the endpoint token "open"
confirmed at the interpreter: sympy.sympify('open') -> <built-in function open>; sympy.latex of it -> '\\mathtt{\\text{<built-in function open>}}'
confirmed at the interpreter: sympy.sympify('closed') -> Symbol('closed')

root_causes.description: The bank is type-blind. For the `inequality` type it prints the raw [lower, upper, endpoint] triple -- '-inf, 5, ...', '8, inf, closed' -- rather than the inequality the problem asked for and the key boxes (x < 5, n >= 8). Even the five entries not mangled by the sympify bug are still a data structure rather than an answer, so the one column a grader scans cannot be used on any of the twelve problems.

root_causes.description: Every one of the twelve problems says 'Solve and graph' and prints its own number line -- worksheet.tex contains 24 tikzpicture environments -- while answer_key.tex contains none. The key states each graph in words ('open circle at 5, shaded to the left'). Half of what each problem asks for is a drawing, and the grader is given no drawn reference for any of them.

improvements.title: _fmt sympifies a data token into Python's open() and prints it in the answer key
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(), stop feeding non-expression tokens to sympify. Match a small allowlist of literal domain tokens first ('open', 'closed', 'oo', '-oo', relations) and return their intended LaTeX directly. For everything else, call sympify with a locals dict and reject any result that is not a sympy Basic instance -- a bare Python callable, module or builtin must fall to the '---' path or raise, never be handed to sympy.latex. Also add \usepackage[T1]{fontenc} or math-mode escaping so a literal < or > in \text can never typeset as an inverted punctuation mark.
improvements.regression_test: Render a verify JSON with {"id": 1, "type": "inequality", "expr": "x + 4 - 9", "relation": "<", "expected": ["-oo", 5, "open"]} and assert the bank line contains neither 'built-in' nor 'mathtt'. Fails today: the line renders '\mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}', exactly as curr-182's key does on five entries.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes Python internals from a printed classroom document. The blast radius is wider than this case: any verify token that happens to name a builtin -- 'min', 'max', 'sum', 'id', 'set', 'all', 'any', 'round' -- currently renders the same way, silently.
improvements.risk: Low. The bank is display text never consumed by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate is unaffected. Tightening sympify's accepted result type could turn a previously rendered exotic expected into '---'; the accompanying gate should warn when that happens rather than fail.

improvements.title: The bank prints raw [lower, upper, endpoint] triples instead of the inequality
improvements.proposed_change: Make render_entry() type-aware. For type `inequality`, reconstruct the inequality from the entry's own var and the triple -- ('-oo', 5, 'open') with var x becomes '$x < 5$', (8, 'oo', 'closed') with var n becomes '$n \ge 8$' -- which is exactly what the key's detailed solutions box. Keep the raw list rendering only as a fallback when the triple cannot be interpreted.
improvements.regression_test: Render {"id": 2, "type": "inequality", "expr": "n - 6 - 2", "relation": ">=", "var": "n", "expected": [8, "oo", "closed"]} and assert the bank line reads '$n \\ge 8$'. Fails today: it reads '8, ∞, closed'.
improvements.expected_impact: Makes the bank usable on all twelve problems of this sheet rather than none of them, and matches the bank to the key's own boxed answers. Applies to every inequality worksheet in the curriculum.
improvements.risk: Low. Reconstruction needs the entry's var, which defaults to x when absent; fall back to the raw triple whenever var is ambiguous so nothing worse than today's output can be produced.

improvements.title: A 'solve and graph' sheet ships a key with no graphs
improvements.proposed_change: When a stem asks the student to graph, plot, sketch or shade, the answer key must print the completed representation. The generator already emits the 24 number-line TikZ figures on the worksheet from the inequality triples; reuse the same routine in the key with the circle style set from the open/closed token and the ray shaded toward the solution. Add a gate requiring a figure environment inside the key's segment for any problem whose stem contains a graphing verb.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Solve and graph x + 4 < 9' with an answer_key.tex whose problem 1 segment is prose only; assert the answer-key gate fails naming the missing figure. Today answer_key.tex for curr-182 has zero figures and answer-key-ak passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Half of what each of these twelve problems asks for is a drawing; today the grader compares a child's drawing against a sentence. Because the triples already encode endpoint and direction, the key's graphs can be generated with no new authoring.
improvements.risk: Low. It costs page space in the key, which is not budget-capped the way the study guide is. The figures are generated from the same verified data as the worksheet's, so they cannot disagree with it.

case_summary: Correctly accepted. Twelve one-step inequalities with a clean facet ramp (add/subtract, multiply/divide, flip-for-a-negative), full endpoint semantics encoded as [lower, upper, open|closed] triples so the circle style and shading direction are machine-recorded rather than left to prose, and two context problems (10 and 11) whose `inequality`-typed entries carry the RELATION the student was asked to write -- the encoding sister cases in this shard were rejected for lacking. Problem 8 separates 'the answer is negative' from 'you divided by a negative' and the key names the wrong rule a student would apply; problem 12's written explanation is declared manual with a desc, the build exits 2, and the key both models the full-credit sentence and rejects the shallow version. All twelve solutions recompute correctly. Two defects remain that the judge understated or missed. First, the Quick Answers bank prints '<built-in function open>' on entries 1, 4, 6, 7 and 9: _fmt() sympifies the endpoint token and sympy.sympify('open') resolves to Python's built-in open function, whose latex is \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}} -- I confirmed the mechanism directly, and the same path would mangle any token named like a builtin. The other seven entries print raw interval triples ('8, ∞, closed') rather than the inequality the key boxes, so the bank is unusable on all twelve problems, not five. Second, every stem says 'Solve and graph' and worksheet.tex draws 24 number lines while answer_key.tex draws zero, so the grader has prose where a drawn reference belongs.
